## Abstract {.unnumbered}

Accurate progesterone receptor (PR) status is a critical determinant
of endocrine therapy eligibility in breast cancer, yet standard
immunohistochemistry (IHC) exhibits substantial inter-pathologist
variability in diagnostically ambiguous cases. We present a multimodal
clinical decision-support system that integrates RNA-Seq transcriptomic
profiles with whole-slide imaging (WSI) to improve PR status prediction.
To address the mismatch between molecular profiles and variable-length
WSI representations, we introduce an asymmetric cross-attention mechanism
in which the patient's transcriptomic profile guides visual evidence
retrieval from the tissue image with linear computational complexity.
A Cross-Modal Reliability Estimator provides a calibrated per-patient
confidence score to identify cases requiring additional pathologist
review. A normalization-corrected Top-1%-Mass Concentration metric
quantifies attentional focus consistently across slides of any size.

Using the TCGA-BRCA cohort of 951 patients with matched molecular
and imaging data, the model achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.8482 and
PR-AUC of 0.9054. The reliability estimator produces a statistically
robust per-patient confidence score, enabling automated escalation
of discordant cases to pathologist review. Analysis of attention
patterns revealed significant phenotypic separation between
PR-positive and PR-negative tumors (p = 0.018), confirming the
model captures spatial patterns associated with PR phenotype.

Together, these findings demonstrate that genomic-conditioned visual
search is an effective framework for multimodal computational
pathology. The results further show that the measurement instrument,
not the model, determines whether biological signal is recoverable.

## Key Findings {.unnumbered}

::: {.contributions}
- **Genomic-conditioned visual search outperforms unimodal and
  late-fusion baselines** (+0.0801 ROC-AUC), attributable to
  genomic conditioning applied upstream of visual compression,
  at the search stage rather than the pooling stage.
- **PR- tumors show significantly more focal attention than PR+
  tumors** (p = 0.018), consistent with known histopathology
  and learned without spatial supervision.
- **The measurement instrument, not the model, was the bottleneck.**
  Shannon entropy suppresses the phenotypic separation entirely
  (p = 0.401) on the same data; a single normalization step
  recovers it.
- **The gate separates PR+ and PR- patients across the confidence
  spectrum:** 83.1% of concordant cases are PR+ and 67.2% of
  flagged cases are PR-, confirming the reliability estimator
  works as designed.
:::

---

## Limitations {.unnumbered}

Validated on TCGA-BRCA; out-of-distribution performance is
uncharacterized. Gate direction stability requires a
transcriptomically-guided encoder for clinical deployment.
